sources.entry: Agent Workbench by cvelasquez - Local web UI that runs the unmodified Claude Code CLI in a pseudo-terminal and adds tabs, a browsable history of past sessions, conversations rendered as cards, a context meter, and the agent's multiple-choice questions answered from the UI.

summary.one_liner: A local web UI that runs the unmodified Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Antigravity and Pi CLIs in a real terminal and adds tabs, session history, chat-style conversation cards, a context meter, and file, change and note panels around them.
summary.what_it_does: It starts the coding-agent CLI already installed on your machine inside a pseudo-terminal, so everything you type goes straight to the CLI. It keeps several agent tabs open at once, each in its own folder, with a status dot showing working, idle or waiting. A sidebar lists past projects and conversations from every supported CLI, with search, archive and resume. The conversation is rendered as cards with folded tool calls, and a context meter shows token use with a Compact button past 70%. Side panels cover git branches and diffs, a project file tree with previews and editing, rendered plans and documents, a notes scratchpad, and a system console. Optional extras include shared memory between CLIs, a history backup, plan usage-limit display, and remote access over SSH with a phone layout and Android app.
use_cases: Run several coding agents side by side in separate project folders
Resume a past Claude Code or Codex conversation from a sidebar history
Read agent conversations as formatted cards instead of raw terminal output
Watch context window usage and compact a long conversation
Review and merge agent-made git branches from a UI
Use a coding agent from a phone or another computer over an SSH tunnel
how_to_run: agent-workbench  (run from the project folder; opens the browser)
stack: Node.js 20+ (22.13+ for OpenCode and Antigravity history)
notable: Runs the unmodified CLI in a real pseudo-terminal; the app adds UI around it rather than calling an AI API itself
Sessions run on the server, so reloading the browser does not stop a working agent
Answer a CLI's multiple-choice questions from the conversation view (Claude Code and OpenCode)
Parallel work via git worktree branches, each in its own folder, with one-click ff-only merge into main
Server listens only on 127.0.0.1 with a per-start token; remote access is opt-in via SSH tunnel
caveats: Best tested on Windows 11 with PowerShell; macOS and Linux get less daily use per the README
Some features depend on the CLI: questions, plan limits and status line need per-CLI setup or are unavailable for some CLIs
Claude Code plan limits and Antigravity status require editing the CLI's status line settings yourself
Linux install compiles the node-pty native module, requiring python3, make and a C++ compiler
